shared_qualifications: C1: source PREN = wt%Cr + 3.3*wt%Mo for these fabricated Ni-Cr-Mo alloys; the nitrogen term is explicitly omitted (PDF p.81). Table 3.1 (PDF p.104) independently lists all 24 alloy compositions and PRENs. Fig.3.9 (PDF p.101), enlarged panel by panel, supplies temperature and marker coordinates. PREN is an association coordinate, not a measurement of a different composition basis.

PDF p.84 explicitly assigns 600 mV as a plotting surrogate to alloys with no distinct pitting before transpassivity. This source rule plus Table 3.1 composition/PREN and panel temperature supports the corresponding qualitative CRA Transpassive records. Such links are not_comparable numerically: Transpassive is retained literally, never converted into 600 or a pitting bound.

Source specimens are bulk arc-melted alloys, homogenized at 1204 C for 24 h and 1260 C for 42 h then water quenched (PDF p.79), tested by cyclic forward/reverse scans at 2 mV/s against SCE in neutral 0.5 M NaCl (PDF p.80). CRA labels all rows Potentiostatic Polarization, with blank/0.1/0.2/1 scan cells and several incompatible heat treatments and amorphous/nanocrystalline labels. These metadata conflicts are retained; composition/PREN, temperature and source outcome identify the proposed counterparts. Neutral source pH does not establish an exact measured pH of 7.0.

obs_029 and obs_031 retain registry values 580 and 500 mV, respectively. Enlarged Fig.3.9(b) and Fig.3.3 (PDF p.95) instead show about 500 mV at PREN 48.7 and 580 mV at PREN 49.3. Their registry readings appear swapped. Chemistry/coordinate fixes the identities as CRA 629 and 631, with discrepant potential agreement; neither registry reading is repaired.

obs_079 at PREN 49.3 and 90 C is about 570 mV rather than the assigned 600 mV surrogate, whereas CRA 677 says Transpassive. Same alloy/temperature alone does not establish equivalent outcome quantities: this is candidate-only.

The five >0.2 V(SCE) outcomes (obs_097-101) are four-hour potentiostatic-hold limits at 90 C, not the Fig.3.9 scan surrogates. Their shared alloys/medium do not establish that a hold bound is the qualitative scan result.
